prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored OAuth tokens loaded from persistent storage never have `token_expiry_time` restored, so `is_token_valid()` treats an expired stored access token as still valid. This causes the proactive refresh check to be skipped and forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh_token exchange after a client restart. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored OAuth tokens loaded from persistent storage never have `token_expiry_time` restored, so `is_token_valid()` treats an expired stored access token as still valid. This causes the proactive refresh check to be skipped and forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh_token exchange after a client restart. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the actual root cause in `_initialize()` by calling `update_token_expiry()` when stored tokens with `expires_in` are loaded, so `is_token_valid()` and the existing proactive-refresh branch work correctly for every code path that consults token expiry — not just one call site. It's a 4-line change with direct test coverage (new `expired_tokens` fixture/test in test_auth.py). #2875 only patches the symptom reactively inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401-handling branch (adds a 'Step 3.5' that tries `_refresh_token()` before full re-auth), gated behind `can_refresh_token()`; its own comment explicitly attributes the bug to the same missing expiry restoration, meaning it becomes redundant once #1784 lands, while leaving the underlying state (`token_expiry_time` never set) inconsistent for any other consumer of `is_token_valid()`.

prs.author: Dharit13

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same root cause: when SSE reconnection in _handle_reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the client previously just returned silently (the branch was even marked `# pragma: no cover`), leaving the original pending request hanging forever with no error surfaced to the caller. prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2395's diff directly edits the exact MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS bail-out branch and removes its `# pragma: no cover` marker, indicating the failure path is now exercised by a test. PR #3098's diff only adds a generic `_unwrap_exception` helper for pulling a StreamableHTTPError out of an exception tree/group, plus an unrelated `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations` rename; it never shows the bail-out branch itself being touched, so it's a broader, less contained change to exception propagation without the same targeted, test-covered fix at the actual failure site.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same branch in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) handling the case where a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result, but they resolve it in opposite, mutually exclusive ways. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a plain string value for a `str | None`-style parameter that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-encoded string, "null", "123") gets corrupted into a dict/list/int/None instead of being kept as the original string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a plain string value for a `str | None`-style parameter that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-encoded string, "null", "123") gets corrupted into a dict/list/int/None instead of being kept as the original string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a helper to skip JSON pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but the scope differs. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips pre-parsing for ANY union where every member is in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - this also disables JSON coercion for non-str unions like `int | None` or `float | None`, which previously relied on pre-parsing to turn a numeric string into an int/float, so it changes behavior beyond the reported str-corruption bug. #3056's `_is_optional_str` is scoped specifically to `str | None` (Optional[str]) and additionally calls `_unwrap_annotated` on each union member first, so it still correctly detects the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` pattern (documented optional string params) as optional-str; #2032's check compares raw args against a fixed type set and would not match an Annotated-wrapped str, leaving the original bug unfixed for that common pattern.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2962 makes the validator skip the ID-match check entirely when there are no tool_result blocks (`has_tool_results and ...`), citing SEP-1577: a tool_use is NOT required to be followed by a tool_result, so no error should be raised at all. clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to skip JSON pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but the scope differs. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips pre-parsing for ANY union where every member is in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - this also disables JSON coercion for non-str unions like `int | None` or `float | None`, which previously relied on pre-parsing to turn a numeric string into an int/float, so it changes behavior beyond the reported str-corruption bug. #3056's `_is_optional_str` is scoped specifically to `str | None` (Optional[str]) and additionally calls `_unwrap_annotated` on each union member first, so it still correctly detects the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` pattern (documented optional string params) as optional-str; #2032's check compares raw args against a fixed type set and would not match an Annotated-wrapped str, leaving the original bug unfixed for that common pattern.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2962 makes the validator skip the ID-match check entirely when there are no tool_result blocks (`has_tool_results and ...`), citing SEP-1577: a tool_use is NOT required to be followed by a tool_result, so no error should be raised at all.
